pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-04.png with Read and it loaded as an image. I looked at the image itself. Layout: one wide top panel, then two tall panels side by side. My natural reading order: (1) top panel: caption 'Soon, his slot comes up.' at top-left, then the teal screen 'NOW · A-12' at top-right. The ravi face box is upper centre-right and a small meera box sits at the far right edge, both silent. (2) tall left panel: caption 'A quick vitals check first.', then a speech balloon 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' whose tail points down to the nurse face box. The ravi box is lower-left, silent. (3) tall right panel: caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.', the ananya face box in the middle, then the teal screen 'RAVI · READY' near the bottom.
pages.observation: Panel order (wide top panel, then left, then right) is unambiguous. No caption or balloon covers a face box. The nurse balloon's tail ends just above the top edge of the nurse box: very close, but it does not overlap. The tail clearly marks the nurse as the speaker. Issues: (a) 'his slot' opens the page with a pronoun whose referent is on the previous page. 'NOW · A-12' only identifies Ravi if the reader worked out on page 03 that he is A-12. (b) Meera is a tiny, silent box at the panel edge, and her role in the panel (caller? receptionist? fellow patient?) is unclear. (c) The tops of the two tall panels line up, and the right caption sits level with the space between the left caption and the nurse balloon. A reader could jump from 'A quick vitals check first.' to 'Dr. Ananya is notified...' before going back to the nurse's line. The panel border makes this a small risk, not a certain skip. (d) Moving from the vitals station to Dr. Ananya implies a change of place, but neither the text nor the layout marks it. It is also unclear whether 'when he's ready' means 'after vitals are done'. That cause and sequence must be inferred from 'RAVI · READY'. (e) Ravi has no reaction or line anywhere on the page. The nurse greets him and he does not respond, so the exchange feels one-sided. (f) The two tall panels leave large empty lower areas, and only the lone screen display sits in the right one. The space is not linked to any action or reaction (layout observation).
